text:
anya: Heads up ran a longshot load test after the recent preparse refactor. Seeing a subtle p95 regression on tiny-chat workload.

mike: How subtle? numbers?

anya: Baseline vs refactor (tiny chat profile, 20k rps of ~20B messages):
```
baseline: p50 1.6ms, p95 4.8ms
preparse-refactor: p50 1.7ms, p95 6.1ms (+27% tail)
```

sam: Any flamegraph or hotspot?

anya: Uploaded a trimmed stack (host only):
```
host_ingress::tokenize_and_normalize 34%
http2_frame_coalesce 14%
kernel_selector::choose 11%
memcpy 8%
kvcache::probe 7%
other 26%
```

lina: Kernel selector at 11% is surprising. We pinned it down last month. Did the refactor change seq_len detection?

anya: Yesthe refactor moved seq_len rounding later in the pipeline to simplify parsing. That delay makes the kernel selector see more variance in incoming sequence-length histograms and flip kernels more.

zach: Kernel flip churn can cause KV warmup because scratch-layout changes force kvstate reinit. If KV shards are rehashed or even re-bucketed that can drop hit rate. Do we have kvcache telemetry for the run?

perf-bot: Telemetry snapshot: kvcache global hit-rate fell from 94% -> 78% during the refactor test window. Eviction rate +1.8x.

mike: Oof. That aligns with the extra p95. Frequent micro-evictions lead to more kvcache misses that cascade into longer decode paths.

sam: Two quick mitigations we can try: 1) move kernel-selection earlier (recompute seq_len pre-parse) to avoid mid-pipeline flips, or 2) add hysteresis to kernel_choice (require sustained seq_len change or threshold > X tokens). Both are low-risk.

lina: Also look at the http2_frame_coalesce 14%. Are we writing many 100-200B frames? gRPC smallwrite penalty is real on our infra. Could coalescing at host before socket write help?

anya: I experimented with an adaptive coalesce strategy: accumulate small frames up to 512B or 600us delay, whichever first. Results on the same test: p50 1.5ms, p95 5.2ms (improvement vs refactor, but slightly different tradeoff).

zach: Does that delay hurt latency-sensitive single-client flows? We need per-route heuristics.

sam: We should implement per-route adaptive window and a per-tenant disable flag. Also we can route high-priority traffic through non-coalescing path.

perf-bot: Candidate commit a2d5c: "ingress: adaptive-writev coalesce window" submitted. Bench queued on staging-gpu.

mike: Any work on avoiding memcpy in tokenize_and_normalize? 8% memcpy is meaningful for small requests.

anya: I pushed a spike branch that keeps proto buffers as slices and uses zero-copy views during normalization. Local microbench shows memcpy time cut by ~60% and host tokenize time drops ~25% for tiny frames.

lina: That plus kernel hysteresis and adaptive writev sounds promising. But be careful: zero-copy implies lifetime management of underlying buffer; we must ensure slice lifetimes don't cross request boundaries or the KV cache.

sam: Agreed. Add strict sanity checks and a debug-only mode that verifies no dangling refs under stress.

zach: Also watch batching heuristics in the runtime. If host coalescing reduces the number of small requests hitting the runtime, batching patterns change and kernel selection thresholds may need retuning. We should coordinate changes across host and runtime teams.

perf-bot: Coordination note: eng-runtime and eng-platform owners assigned: sam, anya, and zach. Canary rollout plan in PR description required.

dev-bot: Canary scheduled: staging -> canary-5pct at 1839998200 for commit a2d5c.

mike: Let's roll the zero-copy spike and kernel-hysteresis to a canary together, measure kvcache hit-rate, p95, and write syscalls. I'll take the syscall counters/dashboard.

anya: I'll attach raw traces and flamegraphs to the RFC I'm drafting: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/ingress/host-preparse-coalesce-2026 (draft). It will include per-route thresholds and the canary plan.

sam: Add an automated regression test to CI that runs the tiny-chat harness (ENGRT-712). If any PR increases p95 by >10% we block.

zach: Also add a synthetic that pulses seq_len at runtime to emulate kernel-flip churn and assert kvcache stability.

anya: Thanks everyone. Will follow up after the canary completes. :thumbsup:

mike: Thanks  good plan.
